Golam Mohiuddin Shaifullah

ORCID: 0000-0002-8452-4834

Dipartimento di Fisica “G. Occhialini”
Università degli Studi di Milano-Bicocca, Italy
golamshaifullah.github.io

Research: precision pulsar timing · PTA gravitational-wave inference · nanohertz GW astrophysics

Current and previous positions

2020–present — Postdoctoral Researcher
Università degli Studi di Milano-Bicocca, Italy. Postdoctoral supervisor: Prof. Alberto Sesana.

2017–2020 — Postdoctoral Researcher
ASTRON, the Netherlands. Postdoctoral adviser: Dr. Gemma Janssen.

2012–2013 — Senior Research Fellow
University of Pune, India.

2010–2012 — Junior Research Fellow
University of Pune, India.

Education

2013–2017 — Dr. rer. nat. (PhD)
Universität Bielefeld, Germany. Timing and properties of recycled pulsars. PhD supervisor: Prof. Joris Verbiest.

2008–2010 — MSc Physics
Fergusson College, University of Pune, India.

2005–2008 — BSc Physics, Electronics and Mathematics
St Joseph’s College, Bangalore University, India.

Research summary

75 refereed publications · 3,060 citing papers · h-index: 30 · 4 software packages
NASA ADS, October 2026

View publications · View talks

My research spans precision pulsar timing, pulsar astrophysics and nanohertz gravitational-wave science. My early work established how measurement uncertainty, instrumentation and propagation effects enter pulsar-timing experiments, combining long-baseline analysis with an invited review that placed these effects in a common experimental framework.

I subsequently moved from individual timing experiments to international PTA datasets and gravitational-wave inference. I coordinated the EPTA DR2 timing dataset, contributed independent searches and statistical validation for its gravitational-wave background analysis, and developed reproducible high-performance-computing environments and researcher training.

My current programme tests the robustness of PTA inference under realistic statistical, computational and astrophysical conditions. It encompasses cross-sampler validation, realistic supermassive-black-hole-binary injection and recovery, accelerated Bayesian computation, observing-strategy studies, and the interpretation of nanohertz signals in terms of astrophysical and cosmological source populations. Much of this work is carried out by researchers I supervise.

Alongside PTA science, I study pulsars across a broad range of radio frequencies using Arecibo, Effelsberg, the Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope, Parkes, LOFAR, NenuFAR and MeerKAT. This work includes pulsar astrophysics, using pulsars to probe the heliosphere and coronal mass ejections, and searches for dark matter with pulsar polarisation arrays.

Professional recognition and reviewing

  • Awards: RAS Group Achievement Award (EPTA, 2025) and ICBS Frontiers of Science Award (PTA collaborations, 2024).
  • Invited talks: 11, including plenary presentations at Amaldi15 and PONT 2023.
  • Reviewing: Swiss National Science Foundation and GMRT Time Allocation Committee.
  • Invited reviews: Single-author CQG review of the current status of PTA science and a co-authored topical review of measurement uncertainty in PTA experiments.

Research collaboration roles

  • 2026–present — Member, Steering Committee, International Pulsar Timing Array.
  • 2025–present — Co-chair, DDPC Friendly Catalogues and Data Standards, LISA Astrophysics Working Group.
  • 2024–present — Member, Gravitational Wave International Committee.
  • 2022–2025 — Co-chair, Data Combination Working Group, International Pulsar Timing Array.
  • 2022–2024 — Member, Executive Committee, European Pulsar Timing Array.
  • 2017–2024 — Chair, Timing Working Group and IISM Working Group, European Pulsar Timing Array.

Research supervision

  • 2024–present — Postdoctoral researchers (3): accelerated nested sampling, GPU-accelerated PTA analysis and reproducible high-performance PTA workflows.
  • 2023–present — PhD researchers (2): PTA GW inference, eccentric SMBHB signatures, nanohertz GW anisotropy and population-dependent observables.
  • 2018–2021 — PhD projects (3): precision pulsar timing, PTA analysis standards and compact-binary timing.
  • 2021–present — Master’s theses (6): PTA data analysis, robustness of GWB inference, deterministic and stochastic GW signals, continuous sources and eccentric SMBHBs.
  • 2014–2022 — Bachelor’s theses (4) and summer research project (1): pulsar timing, compact objects, scintillation and propagation.
  • 2010–2013 — BE/BTech (3), MSc (4) and MTech (1) projects: approximately 200 hours of project supervision.

Teaching and technical training

  • 2024: Designed and taught a 16-hour PhD course, Stochastic gravitational-wave backgrounds from the nanohertz to the kilohertz, Università degli Studi di Milano-Bicocca.
  • 2022: Delivered researcher training in pulsar analysis with Enterprise, Astronomical Observatory of Cagliari.
  • 2019: Designed and delivered IPTA Student Week tutorials in PSRCHIVE, its Python interface and Tempo2.
  • 2016: Taught regression analysis with Python, Universität Bielefeld.
  • 2010–2013: Designed and delivered 4-credit MSc practical laboratory courses at the University of Pune, comprising approximately 60 contact hours for classes of about 30 students.
  • 2010: Co-designed and delivered an MSc bridge course in electronics at the University of Pune.
  • 2010–2011: Taught a 36-hour Applied Electrodynamics Laboratory course for fourth-year integrated-MSc students.

Research funding and observing time

  • 2026 — Fondo di Ateneo Quota Competitiva, Università degli Studi di Milano-Bicocca, €30,000.
  • 2022 — Co-investigator, PRIN GRAPE, Italian Ministry for Universities and Research; project funding €249,880.
  • 2016–present — Telescope time: 5,222 hours allocated through 22 PI/co-PI proposals with Effelsberg, Arecibo, LOFAR, GMRT and Murriyang/Parkes, including 285 hours as PI.
  • Participation in MeerKAT and NenuFAR observing programmes.

Community and organisational service

  • 2024–present: Member, Diversity, Equity & Inclusion Sub-committee, Gravitational Wave International Committee.
  • 2022–present: Secretary General, Gravitational Wave Early Career Scientists.
  • 2021–present: Founder and Chair, PTA Early Career Scientists Working Group, International Pulsar Timing Array.
  • 2020–present: Organiser of a recurring EPTA forum on mentoring, research practice, remote and hybrid working, work–life balance and neurodiversity.
  • Organising roles in more than 20 workshops and meetings across approximately 17 scientific events, including IPTA Student Weeks, EPTA/IPTA science meetings, the 2025 Early Career Researcher workshop, EAS Symposium S2, the ASTRON/JIVE summer programme, Amaldi16 and gravitational-wave workshops.
